title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (inferred from this and the neighbouring pages). Σ is the Riemann sphere with three marked points. Σ̃ appears to be Σ with small open discs removed around the punctures, the 'circles' in the figure. Its fundamental group is the free profinite (or discrete) group Π_{0,3} on two generators. The real line cuts Σ into two hemispheres; the base points P_ε (ε = ±) sit in them. The points Q_i sit on the three real edges. The points R_i^ω (written R^ω_{ω i} on this page) are points on the boundary circles where edge i meets the circle around a puncture; in modern terms they are tangential base points. On the previous page, choosing an orientation ϖ_+ of Σ selects a canonical 'standard region'. Through a canonical isomorphism Ψ_r, this gives an identification Ψ_i^ω : Π_{0,3} → π_1(Σ̃, R_i^ω), canonical up to the choice of ϖ_+.

This page:
- The orientation identifies the index sets ω and ε, so P_ω may be written for P_ε.
- Diagram (44) is commutative and compares three identifications of Π_{0,3}:
  - Ψ_i^ω with π_1 at the tangential point R;
  - ψ_i^ω with Π_i = π_1(Σ̃, Q_i);
  - ψ_ω^i with Π_ω = π_1(Σ̃, P_ω).
- The bottom row is made of path-conjugation isomorphisms: b_i^{ω'}(·) along the edge, and φ_{iω} = c_i^ω(·) from Q_i to P_ω.

The task is to make explicit how one passes from Π_i^ω = π_1(Σ̃, R^ω) to Π_i^{ω'} = π_1(Σ̃, R^{ω'}). These are the tangential base points at the two ends of edge i. The passage is transport along the path b̃_i^ω, which runs along edge i through Q_i, as in the figure.

Using (44) together with the second formula (39) of an earlier page, Grothendieck obtains (45): b̃_i^ω(Ψ_i^ω(x)) = Ψ_i^{ω'}(τ_∞(x)).
- So the two standard identifications of the fundamental groups at the two ends of an edge differ by a fixed automorphism τ_∞ of Π_{0,3}.
- τ_∞ is presumably the involution of the tripod or sphere that swaps the two endpoints of the edge and fixes the third puncture (in modern coordinates, x ↦ 1−x).

Purpose: this is bookkeeping toward the 'Teichmüller groupoid / Lego' description of Π_{0,3}-valued data. It is preparation for writing the Galois action, or for GT-type relations, in terms of one standard group with explicit transition automorphisms.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The formula is consistent with the standard fact: conjugation along the straight path between the tangential base points at the two ends of an edge corresponds to the order-2 symmetry. Whether τ_∞ is the correct symmetry for an arbitrary edge i (rather than one depending on i) cannot be checked from this page alone. It may be a notational shortcut.

ideas.what: Base points at points of the boundary circles of the real-blown-up sphere (R_i^ω) with canonical identifications to Π_{0,3}, depending on an orientation
ideas.modern_name: Tangential base points; the Teichmüller groupoid in genus 0
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (1989) for tangential base points; Ihara and Drinfeld (c. 1990) for the GT setup; Schneps, Lochak, Nakamura for the Teichmüller groupoid
ideas.where_published: The idea of a 'Lego' Teichmüller groupoid built from base points on the boundary of surfaces is sketched in Esquisse d'un programme (1984). This explicit construction is not published.

ideas.what: Transport along the edge path between the tangential base points at the two ends of an edge equals a fixed automorphism τ_∞ of Π_{0,3}, as in (45)
ideas.modern_name: The 'θ' relation (path 01→10 and the symmetry x ↦ 1−x) underlying the 2-cycle relation f(x,y)f(y,x)=1 in GT

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but routine base-point bookkeeping computation in the genus-0 Teichmüller/Lego setup. It anticipates, in Grothendieck's own notation, the tangential-base-point formalism and the symmetry relation later standard through Deligne, Ihara and Drinfeld. Nothing beyond what that literature contains is visible.
transcription_corrections: 'où on a ficeté P_ω en lieu de P_ε' should most likely read 'où on a écrit P_ω au lieu de P_ε'.

The left vertex of (44) is π_1(Σ̃, R^ω_{ωi}), not R^ω_{ω'i}. On the left arrow Grothendieck crossed out a label 'π_{03}' and wrote Ψ_i^ω.
In the figure the endpoints are labelled R^ω_{ωi} (left) and R^{ω'}_{ωi} (right), with Q_i in the middle and the path labelled b̃_i^ω.
